# Skill: customize-opencode

<!--

# Customizing opencode

opencode validates its own config strictly and refuses to start when a field
is wrong. The shapes below cover the common surface area, but they are a
**summary, not the source of truth**.

## Full schema reference

The authoritative list of every config option — with field types, enums,
defaults, and descriptions — lives in the published JSON Schema:

**<https://opencode.ai/config.json>**

If a field is not documented in this skill, or you need to confirm an exact
shape before writing config, **fetch that URL and read the schema directly**
rather than guessing. opencode hard-fails on invalid config, so the cost of a
wrong shape is a broken startup.

Independently, every `opencode.json` should declare
`"$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json"` so the user's editor catches
mistakes as they type.

## Applying changes

Config is loaded once when opencode starts and is not hot-reloaded. After
saving changes to `opencode.json`, an agent file, a skill, a plugin, or any
other config-time file, **tell the user to quit and restart opencode** for
the changes to take effect. The running session will keep using the
already-loaded config until then.

## Where files live

| Scope                         | Path                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Project config                | `./opencode.json`, `./opencode.jsonc`, or `.opencode/opencode.json` (opencode walks up from the cwd to the worktree root) |
| Global config                 | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` or `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (NOT `~/.opencode/`)                            |
| Project agents                | `.opencode/agent/<name>.md` or `.opencode/agents/<name>.md`                                                               |
| Global agents                 | `~/.config/opencode/agent(s)/<name>.md`                                                                                   |
| Project commands              | `.opencode/command/<name>.md` or `.opencode/commands/<name>.md`                                                           |
| Global commands               | `~/.config/opencode/command(s)/<name>.md`                                                                                 |
| Project skills                | `.opencode/skill(s)/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                                                      |
| Global skills                 | `~/.config/opencode/skill(s)/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                                             |
| External skills (auto-loaded) | `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                    |

Configs from each scope are deep-merged. Project overrides global. Unknown
top-level keys in `opencode.json` are rejected with `ConfigInvalidError`.

## opencode.json

Every field is optional.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "username": "string",
  "model": "provider/model-id",
  "small_model": "provider/model-id",
  "default_agent": "agent-name",
  "shell": "/bin/zsh",
  "logLevel": "DEBUG" | "INFO" | "WARN" | "ERROR",
  "share": "manual" | "auto" | "disabled",
  "autoupdate": true | false | "notify",
  "snapshot": true,
  "instructions": ["AGENTS.md", "docs/style.md"],

  "skills": {
    "paths": [".opencode/skills", "/abs/path/to/skills"],
    "urls": ["https://example.com/.well-known/skills/"]
  },

  "references": {
    "docs": {
      "path": "../docs",
      "description": "Use for product behavior and documentation conventions"
    },
    "sdk": {
      "repository": "owner/sdk",
      "branch": "main",
      "description": "Use for SDK implementation details",
      "hidden": true
    }
  },

  "agent": {
    "my-agent": {
      "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6",
      "mode": "subagent",
      "description": "...",
      "permission": { "edit": "deny" }
    }
  },

  "command": {
    "deploy": { "description": "...", "template": "..." }
  },

  "provider": {
    "anthropic": { "options": { "apiKey": "..." } }
  },
  "disabled_providers": ["openai"],
  "enabled_providers": ["anthropic"],

  "mcp": {
    "playwright": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "@playwright/mcp"],
      "enabled": true,
      "environment": {}
    },
    "remote-thing": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://...",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ..." }
    }
  },

  "plugin": [
    "opencode-gemini-auth",
    "opencode-foo@1.2.3",
    "./local-plugin.ts",
    ["opencode-bar", { "option": "value" }]
  ],

  "permission": {
    "edit": "deny",
    "bash": { "git *": "allow", "*": "ask" }
  },

  "formatter": false,
  "lsp": false,

  "experimental": {
    "primary_tools": ["edit"],
    "mcp_timeout": 30000
  },

  "tool_output": { "max_lines": 200, "max_bytes": 8192 },

  "compaction": { "auto": true, "tail_turns": 15 }
}
```

Shape notes worth being explicit about:

- `model` always carries a provider prefix: `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"`.
- `skills` is an object with `paths` and/or `urls`, not an array.
- `references` is an object keyed by alias. Each value is a local path, Git repository, or string shorthand.
- `agent` is an object keyed by agent name, not an array.
- `command` is an object keyed by command name, not an array.
- `plugin` is an array of strings or `[name, options]` tuples, not an object.
- `mcp[name].command` is an array of strings, never a single string. `type` is required.
- `permission` is either a string action or an object keyed by tool name.

## Skills

opencode's skill loader scans for `**/SKILL.md` inside skill directories. The
file is named `SKILL.md` exactly, and lives in its own folder named after the
skill:

```
.opencode/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md
```

Frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: my-skill
description: One sentence covering what this skill does AND when to trigger it. Front-load the literal keywords or filenames the user is likely to say.
---

# My Skill

(skill body in markdown: instructions, examples, references)
```

- `name` is required, lowercase hyphen-separated, up to 64 chars, and matches the folder name.
- `description` is effectively required: skills without one are filtered out and never surfaced to the model. Cover both _what_ the skill does and _when_ to use it. Write in third person ("Use when...", not "I help with..."). Front-load concrete trigger keywords and filenames; gate with "Use ONLY when..." if the skill should stay quiet on adjacent topics.
- Optional: `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata` (string-string map).

Register skills from non-default locations via `skills.paths` (scanned
recursively for `**/SKILL.md`) and `skills.urls` (each URL serves a list of
skills).

## References

References make local directories and Git repositories outside the active
project available as supporting context. Configure them under `references`,
keyed by the alias used in `@` autocomplete:

```json
{
  "references": {
    "docs": {
      "path": "../product-docs",
      "description": "Use for product behavior and terminology"
    },
    "effect": {
      "repository": "Effect-TS/effect",
      "branch": "main",
      "description": "Use for Effect implementation details"
    }
  }
}
```

Local `path` values may be relative to the declaring config, absolute, or use
`~/`. Git `repository` values accept Git URLs, host/path references, and GitHub
`owner/repo` shorthand; `branch` is optional. Both forms support optional
`description` and `hidden` fields.

- Only references with a `description` are advertised to agents in system context.
- `hidden: true` removes a reference from TUI `@` autocomplete only. It remains available to agents and by direct path.
- Reference directories are automatically allowed through the external-directory boundary; normal read/edit/tool permissions still apply.
- String shorthand is supported: use `"docs": "../docs"` for local paths or `"effect": "Effect-TS/effect"` for Git repositories.

## Agents

Two ways to define an agent. Use the file form for anything non-trivial.

### Inline (in `opencode.json`)

```json
{
  "agent": {
    "my-reviewer": {
      "description": "Reviews PRs for style violations.",
      "mode": "subagent",
      "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6",
      "permission": { "edit": "deny", "bash": "ask" },
      "prompt": "You are a strict PR reviewer..."
    }
  }
}
```

### File

```
.opencode/agent/my-reviewer.md      OR     .opencode/agents/my-reviewer.md
```

```markdown
---
description: Reviews PRs for style violations.
mode: subagent
model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
permission:
  edit: deny
  bash: ask
---

You are a strict PR reviewer. Focus on...
```

The file body becomes the agent's `prompt`. Do not also put `prompt:` in the
frontmatter.

`mode` is one of `"primary"`, `"subagent"`, `"all"`.

Allowed top-level frontmatter fields: `name, model, variant, description, mode,
hidden, color, steps, options, permission, disable, temperature, top_p`. Any
unknown field is silently routed into `options`.

To disable a built-in agent: `agent: { build: { disable: true } }`, or in a
file, `disable: true` in frontmatter.

`default_agent` must point to a non-hidden, primary-mode agent.

### Built-in agents

opencode ships with `build`, `plan`, `general`, `explore`. Hidden internal agents:
`compaction`, `title`, `summary`. To override a built-in's fields, define the
same key in `agent: { <name>: { ... } }`.

## Commands

opencode's command loader scans for `**/*.md` inside command directories. The
file is named after the command, and lives directly inside the `command` folder:

```
.opencode/command/deploy.md
```

Frontmatter:

```markdown
---
description: One sentence describing what the command does.
agent: build
model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
---

(command body in markdown: the prompt opencode runs, with $ARGUMENTS for the user's input)
```

- `template` is the command body — everything below the frontmatter — and is required: it is the prompt opencode runs when the command is invoked. Do not also put a `template:` key in the frontmatter.
- `$ARGUMENTS` is replaced with everything the user typed after the command; `$1`, `$2`, … pull individual positional arguments.
- Optional: `description`, `agent`, `model`, `variant`, `subtask`.

## Plugins

`plugin:` is an array. Each entry is one of:

```json
"plugin": [
  "opencode-gemini-auth",            // npm spec, latest
  "opencode-foo@1.2.3",              // npm spec, pinned
  "./local-plugin.ts",               // file path, relative to the declaring config
  "file:///abs/path/plugin.js",      // file URL
  ["opencode-bar", { "key": "val" }] // tuple form with options
]
```

Auto-discovered plugins (no config entry needed): any `*.ts` or `*.js` file in
`.opencode/plugin/` or `.opencode/plugins/`.

A plugin module exports `default` (or any named export) of type
`Plugin = (input: PluginInput, options?) => Promise<Hooks>`. The export is a
function, not a plain object literal, and the function returns an object
(return `{}` if there is nothing to register).

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"

export default (async ({ client, project, directory, $ }) => {
  return {
    config: (cfg) => {
      // cfg is the live merged config; mutate fields here.
    },
    "tool.execute.before": async (input, output) => {
      // mutate output.args before the tool runs
    },
  }
}) satisfies Plugin
```

Hook surface (mutate `output` in place; return `void`):

- `event(input)`: every bus event
- `config(cfg)`: once on init with the merged config
- `chat.message`, `chat.params`, `chat.headers`
- `tool.execute.before`, `tool.execute.after`
- `tool.definition`
- `command.execute.before`
- `shell.env`
- `permission.ask`
- `experimental.chat.messages.transform`, `experimental.chat.system.transform`,
  `experimental.session.compacting`, `experimental.compaction.autocontinue`,
  `experimental.text.complete`

Special object-shaped (not callbacks): `tool: { my_tool: { ... } }`,
`auth: { ... }`, `provider: { ... }`.

## MCP servers

`mcp:` is an object keyed by server name. Each server is discriminated by
`type`:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "playwright": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "@playwright/mcp"],
      "enabled": true,
      "environment": { "BROWSER": "chromium" }
    },
    "github": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://...",
      "enabled": true,
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {env:GITHUB_TOKEN}" }
    },
    "old-server": { "enabled": false }
  }
}
```

`command` is an array of strings. `environment` sets environment variables for
a local MCP server. `type` is required. Use `enabled: false` to
disable a server inherited from a parent config. String values such as header
tokens support `{env:VAR}` interpolation (and `{file:path}`); the shell-style
`${VAR}` is not substituted.

## Permissions

```json
"permission": {
  "edit": "deny",
  "bash": { "git *": "allow", "rm *": "deny", "*": "ask" },
  "external_directory": { "~/secrets/**": "deny", "*": "allow" }
}
```

Actions: `"allow"`, `"ask"`, `"deny"`.

Per-tool value forms: `"allow"` shorthand (treated as `{"*": "allow"}`), or an
object `{ pattern: action }`. Within an object, **insertion order matters**.
opencode evaluates the LAST matching rule, so put broad rules first and narrow
rules last.

`permission: "allow"` (a string at the top level) is shorthand for "allow
everything" and is rarely what the user wants.

Known permission keys: `read, edit, glob, grep, list, bash, task,
external_directory, todowrite, question, webfetch, websearch, lsp, doom_loop,
skill`. Some of these (`todowrite,
question, webfetch, websearch, doom_loop`) only accept a flat
action, not a per-pattern object.

`external_directory` patterns are filesystem paths (use `~/`, absolute paths,
or globs like `~/projects/**`).

Per-agent `permission:` overrides top-level `permission:`. Plan Mode lives on
the `plan` agent's permission ruleset (`edit: deny *`).

## Escape hatches

When a user's config is broken and opencode won't start, these env vars help:

- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1`: skip the project's local `opencode.json`
  and start from globals only. Run from the project directory, opencode loads,
  the user edits the broken file, then they restart without the flag.
- `OPENCODE_CONFIG=/path/to/file.json`: load an additional explicit config.
- `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='{"$schema":"https://opencode.ai/config.json"}'`:
  inject inline JSON as a final local-scope merge.
- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS=1`: skip default plugins.
- `OPENCODE_PURE=1`: skip external plugins entirely.
- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS=1`,
  `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS=1`: skip the external skill scans under
  `~/.claude/` and `~/.agents/`.

## When proposing edits

- Validate against the schema before writing. If you are unsure of a field's
  exact shape, or the field is not covered in this skill, fetch
  `https://opencode.ai/config.json` and read the schema rather than guessing.
- Preserve `$schema` and any existing fields the user did not ask to change.
- For agent, command, skill, and plugin definitions, prefer creating new files
  in the correct location over inlining everything in `opencode.json`.
- If the user's existing config is malformed, point them at the env-var escape
  hatches above so they can edit from inside opencode without breaking their
  session.
- After saving any config change, remind the user to quit and restart opencode
  — running sessions keep using the already-loaded config.

Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.

241:                 self.unbounded_log_instance@,
242:             ),
243:             self.wf(self.thread_id_g@),
244:         ensures
245:             res.1@.enqueue_op_post(context_ghost@),
246:             res.1@.cell_id == self.batch.0.id(),
247:             self.wf(self.thread_id_g@),
248:     {
249:         let tracked FCClientRequestResponseGhost {
250:             batch_perms: batch_perms,
251:             cell_id,
252:             local_updates: local_updates,
253:             fc_clients: mut fc_clients,
254:         } = context_ghost.get();
255:         let tracked mut batch_perms = batch_perms.tracked_unwrap();
256:         let tracked local_updates = local_updates.tracked_unwrap();
257:         self.batch.0.put(Tracked(&mut batch_perms), PendingOperation::new(op));
258:         let tracked send_request_result;
259:         let res =
260:             atomic_with_ghost!(
261:             &self.atomic.0 => store(1);
262:             update prev->next;
263:             ghost g => {
264:                 let ghost tid = fc_clients.key();
265:                 let ghost rid = local_updates.key();
266: 
267:                 self.flat_combiner_instance.borrow().pre_send_request(tid, &fc_clients, &g.slots);
268:                 send_request_result = self.flat_combiner_instance.borrow().send_request(tid, rid, fc_clients, g.slots);
269:                 fc_clients = send_request_result.0.get();
270: 
271:                 g.slots = send_request_result.1.get();
272:                 g.batch_perms = Some(batch_perms);
273:                 g.update = Some(local_updates);
274: 
275:                 assert(g.inv(1, tid, self.batch.0, self.flat_combiner_instance.view(), self.unbounded_log_instance.view()))
276:             }
277:         );
278:         let tracked new_context_ghost = FCClientRequestResponseGhost {
279:             batch_perms: None,
280:             cell_id,
281:             local_updates: None,
282:             fc_clients,
283:         };
284:         (true, Tracked(new_context_ghost))
285:     }
286: 
287:     pub fn dequeue_response(
288:         &self,
289:         context_ghost: Tracked<FCClientRequestResponseGhost<DT>>,
290:     ) -> (res: (Option<DT::Response>, Tracked<FCClientRequestResponseGhost<DT>>))
291:         requires
292:             context_ghost@.dequeue_resp_pre(
293:                 self.batch.0.id(),
294:                 self.thread_id_g@,
295:                 self.flat_combiner_instance@,
296:             ),
297:             self.wf(self.thread_id_g@),
298:         ensures
299:             res.1@.dequeue_resp_post(context_ghost@, res.0, self.unbounded_log_instance@),
300:             self.wf(self.thread_id_g@),
301:     {
302:         let tracked FCClientRequestResponseGhost {
303:             batch_perms: mut batch_perms,
304:             cell_id,
305:             local_updates: mut local_updates,
306:             fc_clients: mut fc_clients,
307:         } = context_ghost.get();
308:         let tracked recv_response_result;
309:         let res =
310:             atomic_with_ghost!(
311:             &self.atomic.0 => load();
312:             returning res;
313:             ghost g => {
314:                 if res == 0 {
315:                     batch_perms = g.batch_perms;
316:                     local_updates = g.update;
317: 
318:                     let tid = fc_clients.key();
319:                     let rid = fc_clients.value().get_Waiting_0();
320:                     self.flat_combiner_instance.borrow().pre_recv_response(tid, &fc_clients, &g.slots);
321:                     recv_response_result = self.flat_combiner_instance.borrow().recv_response(tid, rid, fc_clients, g.slots);
322:                     fc_clients = recv_response_result.0.get();
323: 
324:                     g.slots = recv_response_result.1.get();
325:                     g.batch_perms = None;
326:                     g.update = None;
327:                 }
328:             }
329:         );
330:         if res == 0 {
331:             let tracked mut batch_perms = batch_perms.tracked_unwrap();
332:             let op = self.batch.0.take(Tracked(&mut batch_perms));
333:             let resp = op.resp.unwrap();
334:             let tracked new_context_ghost = FCClientRequestResponseGhost {
335:                 batch_perms: Some(batch_perms),
336:                 cell_id,
337:                 local_updates,
338:                 fc_clients,
339:             };
340:             (Some(resp), Tracked(new_context_ghost))
341:         } else {
342:             let tracked new_context_ghost = FCClientRequestResponseGhost {
343:                 batch_perms,
344:                 cell_id,
345:                 local_updates,
346:                 fc_clients,
347:             };
348:             (None, Tracked(new_context_ghost))
349:         }
350:     }

359: struct_with_invariants!{
360: pub tracked struct ContextGhost<DT: Dispatch> {
361:     pub batch_perms: Option<PointsTo<PendingOperation<DT>>>,
362: 
363:     pub slots: FlatCombiner::slots,
364: 
365:     pub update: Option<UnboundedLog::local_updates<DT>>
366: }
367: 
368: pub open spec fn inv(&self, v: u64, tid: nat, cell: PCell<PendingOperation<DT>>, fc: FlatCombiner::Instance, inst: UnboundedLog::Instance<DT>) -> bool {
369:     predicate {
370:         &&& self.slots.key() == tid
371:         &&& self.slots.instance_id() == fc.id()
372: 
373:         &&& ((v == 0) || (v == 1))
374:         &&& (v == 0 ==> self.slots.value().is_Empty() || self.slots.value().is_Response())
375:         &&& (v == 1 ==> self.slots.value().is_Request() || self.slots.value().is_InProgress())
376: 
377:         &&& (self.slots.value().is_Empty() ==> {
378:             &&& self.update.is_none()
379:             &&& self.batch_perms.is_none()
380:         })
381: 
382:         &&& (self.slots.value().is_Request() ==> {
383:             &&& self.update matches Some(update)
384:             &&& update.value().is_Init()
385:             &&& update.key() == self.slots.value().get_ReqId()
386:             &&& update.instance_id() == inst.id()
387: 
388:             &&& self.batch_perms matches Some(batch_perms)
389:             &&& batch_perms.mem_contents().is_init()
390:             &&& batch_perms@.pcell == cell.id()
391:             &&& batch_perms.mem_contents().value().op == update.value().get_Init_op()
392:         })
393: 
394:         &&& (self.slots.value().is_InProgress() ==> {
395:             &&& self.update.is_none()
396:             &&& self.batch_perms.is_none()
397:         })
398: 
399:         &&& (self.slots.value().is_Response() ==> {
400:             &&& self.update matches Some(update)
401:             &&& update.value().is_Done()
402:             &&& update.key() == self.slots.value().get_ReqId()
403:             &&& update.instance_id() == inst.id()
404: 
405:             &&& self.batch_perms matches Some(batch_perms)
406:             &&& batch_perms.mem_contents().is_init()
407:             &&& batch_perms@.pcell == cell.id()
408:             &&& batch_perms.mem_contents().value().resp matches Some(resp)
409:             &&& resp == update.value().get_Done_ret()
410:         })
411:     }
412: }
413: }

416: pub tracked struct FCClientRequestResponseGhost<DT: Dispatch> {
417:     pub tracked batch_perms: Option<PointsTo<PendingOperation<DT>>>,
418:     pub tracked cell_id: Ghost<CellId>,
419:     pub tracked local_updates: Option<UnboundedLog::local_updates<DT>>,
420:     pub tracked fc_clients: FlatCombiner::clients,
421: }
422: 
423: impl<DT: Dispatch> FCClientRequestResponseGhost<DT> {
424:     pub open spec fn enqueue_op_pre(
425:         &self,
426:         tid: nat,
427:         op: DT::WriteOperation,
428:         batch_cell: CellId,
429:         fc_inst: FlatCombiner::Instance,
430:         inst: UnboundedLog::Instance<DT>,
431:     ) -> bool {
432:         &&& self.local_updates matches Some(local_updates)
433:         &&& local_updates.instance_id() == inst.id()
434:         &&& local_updates.value().is_Init()
435:         &&& local_updates.value().get_Init_op() == op
436:         &&& self.batch_perms matches Some(batch_perms)
437:         &&& batch_perms@.pcell == self.cell_id
438:         &&& self.cell_id == batch_cell
439:         &&& batch_perms.mem_contents().is_uninit()
440:         &&& self.fc_clients.instance_id() == fc_inst.id()
441:         &&& self.fc_clients.key() == tid
442:         &&& self.fc_clients.value().is_Idle()
443:     }
444: 
445:     pub open spec fn enqueue_op_post(&self, pre: FCClientRequestResponseGhost<DT>) -> bool
446:         recommends
447:             pre.local_updates.is_some(),
448:     {
449:         &&& self.fc_clients.value().is_Waiting()
450:         &&& self.fc_clients.value().get_Waiting_0() == pre.local_updates.unwrap().key()
451:         &&& self.fc_clients.instance_id() == pre.fc_clients.instance_id()
452:         &&& self.fc_clients.key() == pre.fc_clients.key()
453:         &&& self.cell_id == pre.cell_id
454:         &&& self.batch_perms.is_none()
455:         &&& self.local_updates.is_none()
456:     }
457: 
458:     pub open spec fn dequeue_resp_pre(
459:         &self,
460:         batch_cell: CellId,
461:         tid: nat,
462:         fc_inst: FlatCombiner::Instance,
463:     ) -> bool {
464:         &&& self.fc_clients.key() == tid
465:         &&& self.fc_clients.instance_id() == fc_inst.id()
466:         &&& self.fc_clients.value().is_Waiting()
467:         &&& self.batch_perms.is_none()
468:         &&& self.local_updates.is_none()
469:         &&& self.cell_id == batch_cell
470:     }
471: 
472:     pub open spec fn dequeue_resp_post(
473:         &self,
474:         pre: FCClientRequestResponseGhost<DT>,
475:         ret: Option<DT::Response>,
476:         inst: UnboundedLog::Instance<DT>,
477:     ) -> bool {
478:         &&& ret matches Some(ret) ==> {
479:             &&& self.cell_id == pre.cell_id
480:             &&& self.batch_perms matches Some(batch_perms)
481:             &&& batch_perms.mem_contents().is_uninit()
482:             &&& batch_perms@.pcell == self.cell_id
483:             &&& self.local_updates matches Some(local_updates)
484:             &&& local_updates.instance_id() == inst.id()
485:             &&& local_updates.value().is_Done()
486:             &&& local_updates.key() == pre.fc_clients.value().get_Waiting_0()
487:             &&& local_updates.value().get_Done_ret() == ret
488:             &&& self.fc_clients.instance_id() == pre.fc_clients.instance_id()
489:             &&& self.fc_clients.key() == pre.fc_clients.key()
490:             &&& self.fc_clients.value().is_Idle()
491:         }
492:         &&& ret.is_none() ==> {
493:             &&& self == pre
494:         }
495:     }
496: }
497: 
498: } 
499: }

4441:     s: SState<DT>,

4445:     &&& (0 <= s.version && s.version

4449:     )

4451:     &&& s.readonly_reqs.dom().disjoint(s.update_resps.dom())
4452:     &&& s.update_reqs.dom().disjoint(s.update_resps.dom())
4453:     &&& t.reqs.dom().disjoint(
4454:         t.resps.dom(),
4455:     )
4456:     &&& (forall|rid|
4457:         (#[trigger] s.readonly_reqs.contains_key(rid) || #[trigger] s.update_reqs.contains_key(rid)
4458:             || #[trigger] s.update_resps.contains_key(rid)) <==> (#[trigger] t.reqs.contains_key(
4459:             rid,
4460:         ) || #[trigger] t.resps.contains_key(
4461:             rid,
4462:         )))
4463:     &&& (forall|rid| #[trigger]
4464:         t.reqs.contains_key(rid) && #[trigger] t.reqs[rid].is_Read()
4465:             ==> s.readonly_reqs.contains_key(rid))
4466:     &&& (forall|rid| #[trigger]
4467:         t.reqs.contains_key(rid) && #[trigger] t.reqs[rid].is_Write()
4468:             ==> s.update_reqs.contains_key(rid) || s.update_resps.contains_key(rid))
4469:     &&& (forall|rid| #[trigger]
4470:         t.resps.contains_key(rid) ==> s.readonly_reqs.contains_key(rid)
4471:             || s.update_resps.contains_key(
4472:             rid,
4473:         ))
4474:     &&& (forall|v: LogIdx|
4475:         s.version <= v && v < s.log.len() ==> update_response_with_version(
4476:             s.update_resps,
4477:             v,
4478:         ))
4479:     &&& (forall|rid1, rid2| #[trigger]
4480:         s.update_resps.contains_key(rid1) && #[trigger] s.update_resps.contains_key(rid2) && rid1
4481:             != rid2 ==> s.update_resps[rid1]
4482:             != s.update_resps[rid2])
4483:     &&& (forall|rid| #[trigger]
4484:         s.update_resps.contains_key(rid) ==> s.update_resps[rid].0
4485:             < s.log.len())
4486:     &&& (forall|rid| #[trigger]
4487:         s.update_reqs.contains_key(rid) ==> t.reqs.contains_key(rid) && t.reqs[rid]
4488:             == InputOperation::<DT>::Write(
4489:             s.update_reqs[rid],
4490:         ))
4491:     &&& (forall|rid| #[trigger]
4492:         s.update_resps.contains_key(rid) && s.update_resps[rid].0 >= s.version ==> {
4493:             &&& t.reqs.contains_key(rid)
4494:             &&& t.reqs[rid] == InputOperation::<DT>::Write(s.log[s.update_resps[rid].0 as int])
4495:         })
4496:     &&& (forall|rid| #[trigger]
4497:         s.update_resps.contains_key(rid) && s.update_resps[rid].0 < s.version
4498:             ==> update_response_is_valid(s, t, r_points, rid))
4499: }

5066: pub open spec fn compute_nrstate_at_version<DT: Dispatch>(
5067:     log: Seq<DT::WriteOperation>,
5068:     version: LogIdx,
5069: ) -> DT::View
5070:     recommends
5071:         0 <= version <= log.len(),
5072:     decreases version,
5073: {
5074:     if version == 0 {
5075:         DT::init_spec()
5076:     } else {
5077:         DT::dispatch_mut_spec(
5078:             compute_nrstate_at_version::<DT>(log, (version - 1) as nat),
5079:             log[version - 1],
5080:         ).0
5081:     }
5082: }

7814: verus! {
7815: 
7816: tokenized_state_machine!{
7817:     #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, verifier::reject_recursive_types(T))]
7818:     RwLockSpec<T> {
7819:         fields {
7820:             #[sharding(constant)]
7821:             pub user_inv: ISet<T>,
7822: 
7823:             #[sharding(constant)]
7824:             pub rc_width: int,
7825: 
7826:             #[sharding(storage_option)]
7827:             pub storage: Option<T>,
7828: 
7829:             #[sharding(variable)]
7830:             pub exc_locked: bool,
7831: 
7832:             #[sharding(map)]
7833:             pub ref_counts: Map<int, int>,
7834: 
7835:             #[sharding(option)]
7836:             pub exc_pending: Option<int>,
7837: 
7838:             #[sharding(option)]
7839:             pub exc_guard: Option<()>,
7840: 
7841:             #[sharding(multiset)]
7842:             pub shared_pending: Multiset<int>,
7843: 
7844:             #[sharding(multiset)]
7845:             pub shared_guard: Multiset<(int, T)>,
7846:         }
7847: 
7848:         init!{
7849:             initialize(rc_width: int, init_t: T, user_inv: ISet<T>,) {
7850:                 require(0 < rc_width);
7851:                 require(user_inv.contains(init_t));
7852:                 init rc_width = rc_width;
7853:                 init user_inv = user_inv;
7854:                 init storage = Option::Some(init_t);
7855:                 init exc_locked = false;
7856:                 init ref_counts = Map::new(
7857:                     Set::range(0, rc_width),
7858:                     |i| 0,
7859:                 );
7860:                 init exc_pending = Option::None;
7861:                 init exc_guard = Option::None;
7862:                 init shared_pending = Multiset::empty();
7863:                 init shared_guard = Multiset::empty();
7864:             }
7865:         }
7866: 
7867:         transition!{
7868:             exc_start() {
7869:                 require(!pre.exc_locked);
7870:                 update exc_locked = true;
7871:                 add exc_pending += Some(0);
7872:             }
7873:         }
7874: 
7875:         transition!{
7876:             exc_check_count() {
7877:                 remove exc_pending -= Some(let r);
7878:                 have ref_counts >= [r => 0];
7879: 
7880:                 add exc_pending += Some(r + 1);
7881:             }
7882:         }
7883: 
7884:         transition!{
7885:             exc_finish() {
7886:                 remove exc_pending -= Some(pre.rc_width);
7887:                 add exc_guard += Some(());
7888: 
7889:                 birds_eye let x = pre.storage.unwrap();
7890: 
7891:                 withdraw storage -= Some(x);
7892:                 assert(pre.user_inv.contains(x));
7893:             }
7894:         }
7895: 
7896:         transition!{
7897:             exc_release(t: T) {
7898:                 require(pre.user_inv.contains(t));
7899:                 update exc_locked = false;
7900:                 remove exc_guard -= Some(());
7901:                 deposit storage += Some(t);
7902:             }
7903:         }
7904: 
7905:         transition!{
7906:             shared_start(r: int) {
7907:                 remove ref_counts -= [r => let rc];
7908:                 add ref_counts += [r => rc + 1];
7909:                 add shared_pending += {r};
7910:             }
7911:         }
7912: 
7913:         transition!{
7914:             shared_abandon(r: int) {
7915:                 remove ref_counts -= [r => let rc];
7916:                 require(rc > 0);
7917:                 add ref_counts += [r => rc - 1];
7918:                 remove shared_pending -= {r};
7919:             }
7920:         }
7921: 
7922:         transition!{
7923:             shared_finish(r: int) {
7924:                 require(!pre.exc_locked);
7925:                 remove shared_pending -= {r};
7926: 
7927:                 birds_eye let t = pre.storage.unwrap();
7928:                 add shared_guard += {(r, t)};
7929: 
7930:                 assert(pre.user_inv.contains(t));
7931:             }
7932:         }
7933: 
7934:         transition!{
7935:             shared_release(val: (int, T)) {
7936:                 remove shared_guard -= {val};
7937: 
7938:                 let r = val.0;
7939:                 remove ref_counts -= [r => let rc];
7940:                 add ref_counts += [r => rc - 1];
7941: 
7942:                 assert(rc > 0) by {
7943:                     assert(0 <= r < pre.rc_width);
7944:                     assert(pre.shared_guard.count(val) > 0);
7945:                     assert(Self::filter_r(pre.shared_guard, r).count(val) > 0);
7946:                     assert(Self::filter_r(pre.shared_guard, r).len() > 0);
7947:                     assert(pre.ref_counts.index(r) > 0);
7948:                 };
7949:             }
7950:         }
7951: 
7952:         property!{
7953:             do_guard(val: (int, T)) {
7954:                 have shared_guard >= {val};
7955:                 guard storage >= Some(val.1);
7956:             }
7957:         }
7958: 
7959:         property!{
7960:             rc_not_zero_guard(r: int) {
7961:                 have shared_pending >= {r};
7962:                 have ref_counts >= [r => let rc];
7963:                 assert(rc > 0);
7964:             }
7965:         }

7969:         #[invariant]
7970:         pub fn sto_user_inv(&self) -> bool {

7972:                 self.user_inv.contains(storage)
7973:         }
7974: 
7975:         #[invariant]
7976:         pub fn ref_counts_domain(&self) -> bool {
7977:             &&& 0 < self.rc_width
7978:             &&& forall |i: int| 0 <= i < self.rc_width <==> self.ref_counts.dom().contains(i)
7979:         }
7980: 
7981:         #[invariant]
7982:         pub fn exc_inv(&self) -> bool {
7983:             &&& self.exc_locked <==> (self.exc_pending.is_some() || self.exc_guard.is_some())
7984:             &&& self.storage.is_some() <==> self.exc_guard.is_none()

7990:                 true
7991:             }
7992:         }
7993:

7995:         pub fn shared_pending_in_range(&self) -> bool {
7996:             forall |r| self.shared_pending.count(r) > 0 ==> (0 <= r < self.rc_width)
7997:         }
7998: 
7999:         #[invariant]
8000:         pub fn shared_guard_in_range(&self) -> bool {
8001:             forall |x| self.shared_guard.count(x) > 0 ==> (0 <= x.0 < self.rc_width)
8002:         }
8003: 
8004:         #[invariant]
8005:         pub fn shared_inv_agree(&self) -> bool {
8006:             forall |v| #[trigger] self.shared_guard.count(v) > 0 ==>
8007:                 self.storage === Option::Some(v.1)
8008:         }
8009: 
8010:         pub closed spec fn filter_r(shared_guard: Multiset<(int, T)>, r: int) -> Multiset<(int, T)> {
8011:             shared_guard.filter(|val: (int, T)| val.0 == r)
8012:         }
8013: 
8014:         #[invariant]
8015:         pub fn shared_counts_agree(&self) -> bool {
8016:             forall |r| 0 <= r < self.rc_width ==>
8017:                 #[trigger] self.ref_counts.index(r) ==
8018:                     self.shared_pending.count(r) as int +
8019:                         Self::filter_r(self.shared_guard, r).len() as int
8020:         }
8021: 
8022:         #[inductive(initialize)]
8023:         fn initialize_inductive(post: Self, rc_width: int, init_t: T,  user_inv: ISet<T>) {
8024:             assert forall |r| 0 <= r < post.rc_width implies
8025:                 #[trigger] post.ref_counts.index(r) ==
8026:                     post.shared_pending.count(r) as int +
8027:                         Self::filter_r(post.shared_guard, r).len() as int
8028:             by {
8029:                 assert(post.ref_counts.index(r) == 0);
8030:                 assert(post.shared_pending.count(r) == 0);
8031:                 assert(Self::filter_r(post.shared_guard, r) =~= Multiset::empty());
8032:                 assert(Self::filter_r(post.shared_guard, r).len() == 0);
8033:             }
8034:             assert(post.shared_counts_agree());
8035:         }
8036: 
8037:         #[inductive(exc_start)]
8038:         fn exc_start_inductive(pre: Self, post: Self) {
8039: 
8040:         }
8041: 
8042:         #[inductive(exc_check_count)]
8043:         fn exc_check_count_inductive(pre: Self, post: Self) {
8044:             let prev_r = pre.exc_pending.unwrap();
8045:             assert forall |x| #[trigger] post.shared_guard.count(x) > 0
8046:                 && x.0 == prev_r implies false
8047:             by {
8048:                 assert(Self::filter_r(post.shared_guard, prev_r).count(x) > 0);
8049:             }
8050:         }
8051: 
8052:         #[inductive(exc_finish)]
8053:         fn exc_finish_inductive(pre: Self, post: Self) {
8054:         }
8055: 
8056:         #[inductive(exc_release)]
8057:         fn exc_release_inductive(pre: Self, post: Self, t: T) {
8058: 
8059:         }
8060: 
8061:         #[inductive(shared_start)]
8062:         fn shared_start_inductive(pre: Self, post: Self, r: int) { }
8063: 
8064:         #[inductive(shared_abandon)]
8065:         fn shared_abandon_inductive(pre: Self, post: Self, r: int) { }
8066: 
8067:         #[inductive(shared_finish)]
8068:         fn shared_finish_inductive(pre: Self, post: Self, r: int) {
8069:             let t = pre.storage.unwrap();
8070: 
8071:             assert forall |r0| 0 <= r0 < post.rc_width implies
8072:                 #[trigger] post.ref_counts.index(r0) ==
8073:                     post.shared_pending.count(r0) as int +
8074:                         Self::filter_r(post.shared_guard, r0).len() as int
8075:             by {
8076:                 if r == r0 {

8078:                     assert(Self::filter_r(post.shared_guard, r) =~= Self::filter_r(pre.shared_guard, r).add(Multiset::singleton((r, t))));
8079:                     assert(post.ref_counts.index(r0) ==

8081:                             Self::filter_r(post.shared_guard, r0).len() as int);
8082:                 } else {

8084:                     assert(post.ref_counts.index(r0) ==

8088:             }
8089:         }

I need to understand the verification errors in a Verus file. Please analyze the following code sections and figure out what proof annotations are needed in the `atomic_with_ghost!` blocks.

The file is /workspace/task_env/log_full_verified.rs. The errors are at these locations:

1. Line 1190: precondition not satisfied for `advance_tail_abort`
2. Lines 1234-1240: `atomic_with_ghost!` for compare_exchange_weak on tail - invariant not satisfied
3. Line 1270: invariant `cb_combiner.value().get_Appending_cur_idx() == tail + idx` not satisfied at end of loop body
4. Lines 1316-1320: `atomic_with_ghost!` for store on slog[log_idx].alive - invariant not satisfied
5. Lines 1629-1632: invariant before loop not satisfied
6. Lines 1698-1700: invariants about cb_combiner when is_alive in inner while loop
7. Lines 1848-1856 (find_min_local_version): invariant about g_cb_comb_new.value().is_AdvancingHead() and idx before and after loop
8. Line 1468: atomic_with_ghost for head store not satisfied
9. Lines 1389/1567: postcondition not satisfied

Please read the relevant code sections from the file and figure out what transitions or ghost operations need to be added to each `atomic_with_ghost!` block. Look especially at:
- The CyclicBuffer state machine transitions (search for `advance_tail_abort`, `advance_tail_start`, `advance_tail_finish`, `append_flip_bit`, `advance_head_start`, `advance_head_next`, `advance_head_finish`)
- The UnboundedLog state machine
- What ghost tokens are available in each context

Please read line ranges 1130-1370 (append function), 1395-1500 (advance_head function), 1545-1820 (execute function and find_min_local_version) from the file.

Return a detailed analysis of what proof code needs to be added to each atomic_with_ghost block to fix the verification errors.

<task_result>
It's not called from `append`. This means in the `append` function, the UL `update_place_ops_in_log_one` transitions happen at a different point. But based on the flow:

1. `ghost_data.combiner@.value().is_Ready()` — combiner starts Ready
2. After `advance_tail_start` there's some UL transition needed too...

Wait, let me re-read the `append_pre` again:

```
&&& self.combiner@.value().is_Ready()
&&& self.cb_combiner@.value().is_Idle()
```

And `local_updates` start as `Init`. The `update_place_ops_in_log_one` transitions move from `Init → Placed` and advance `UL::tail`. But when do they fire?

Looking at the data flow: `log_entries` is initialized empty at line 1232 and `local_updates` starts as `Init`. After the CAS success, the inner loop at 1257 runs `append_flip_bit` per entry. But for the UL side, the `log_entries` map must be populated *from the UL system*... Let me re-check what `log_entries` is in the loop invariant:

```rust
forall|i|
    idx <= i < request_ids@.len() ==> {
        &&& (#[trigger] log_entries.contains_key(i))
        &&& log_entries[i].key() == tail + i
        &&& log_entries[i].instance_id() == self.unbounded_log_instance@.id()
```

So `log_entries[i]` are `UnboundedLog::log<DT>` tokens (entries in the UL log). These must come from *firing* `update_place_ops_in_log_one` which places the op into the log and returns the log entry token.

So: the UL placement must happen somewhere before/during the CAS. Looking at the loop invariant requirement (`log_entries` starts empty at line 1232 and must be fully populated before the inner loop at 1257), the UL ops must be placed inside the CAS `atomic_with_ghost!` block when the CAS succeeds!

This is a key design choice: on successful CAS, we fire all `nops` UL `update_place_ops_in_log_one` transitions to place all ops atomically, getting log entry tokens and updating the UL tail from `tail` to `new_tail = tail + nops`. Then `cb_combiner` transitions via `advance_tail_finish`.

**Complete fix for CAS block (lines 1234-1240):**

```rust
let result =
    atomic_with_ghost!(
    &self.tail.0 => compare_exchange_weak(tail, new_tail);
    update prev -> next;
    returning result;
    ghost g => {
        // g: (UnboundedLog::tail<DT>, CyclicBuffer::tail<DT>)
        let tracked (mut ul_tail, mut cb_tail) = g;
        if prev == tail {
            // CAS succeeded: new atomic value is new_tail
            // 1. Place all nops operations into the UL log, incrementing UL tail
            //    from tail to new_tail. This also moves combiner from Ready -> Placed
            //    and populates log_entries.
            let tracked init_state = AppendEntriesGhostState { ... };
            let tracked result_state = self.unbounded_log_append_entries(
                nid as nat, (nops - 1) as nat, init_state);
            log_entries = result_state.log_entries;
            combiner = result_state.combiner;
            ul_tail = result_state.tail;
            local_updates = result_state.local_updates;
            // 2. Fire CB advance_tail_finish: AdvancingTail -> Appending
            //    withdrawing cb_log_entries for the old slots
            let tracked (new_cb_combiner, withdrawn, new_cb_tail) =
                self.cyclic_buffer_instance.borrow().advance_tail_finish(
                    nid as nat, new_tail as nat, cb_combiner, cb_tail);
            cb_combiner = new_cb_combiner;
            cb_log_entries = withdrawn;
            cb_tail = new_cb_tail;
        } else {
            // CAS failed: abort both UL and CB advances
            cb_combiner = self.cyclic_buffer_instance.borrow().advance_tail_abort(
                nid as nat, cb_combiner);
            // UL combiner stays Ready (no transition happened)
        }
        g = (ul_tail, cb_tail);
    }
);
```

After this: `cb_combiner.value() == Appending { cur_idx: tail, tail: new_tail }` which satisfies the loop invariant at line 1270 with `idx == 0`.

---

### Error 3 — Line 1270: `cb_combiner.value().get_Appending_cur_idx() == tail + idx` not satisfied at end of loop body

**Location:** The inner `while idx < nops` loop body, at the end after `atomic_with_ghost!` for `store(m)`.

**Problem:** The `slog[log_idx].alive` store (lines 1316-1320) does not fire `append_flip_bit`, so `cb_combiner` is not updated from `Appending { cur_idx: tail+idx, tail: new_tail }` to `Appending { cur_idx: tail+idx+1, tail: new_tail }`. After `idx = idx + 1` at line 1321, the invariant `cur_idx == tail + idx` requires `cur_idx` to have been incremented.

**Fix needed in `store(m)` block (lines 1316-1320):**

```rust
atomic_with_ghost!(
    &self.slog[log_idx].alive => store(m);
    ghost g => {
        // g: CyclicBuffer::alive_bits<DT> for slot log_idx
        // Fire append_flip_bit: advances cb_combiner cur_idx by 1
        // deposits the StoredType into CB contents
        let tracked stored = StoredType {
            cell_perms: cb_log_entry_perms,
            log_entry: stored_entry_for_this_slot,
        };
        // We need the UL log entry token for this slot
        let tracked ul_log_entry = log_entries.tracked_remove(idx as nat);
        let tracked stored_type = StoredType {
            cell_perms: cb_log_entry_perms,
            log_entry: Option::Some(ul_log_entry),
        };
        cb_combiner = self.cyclic_buffer_instance.borrow().append_flip_bit(
            nid as nat,
            stored_type,
            cb_combiner,
            g,
        );
    }
);
```

`append_flip_bit` requires:
- `combiner[nid] == Appending { cur_idx, tail }` with `cur_idx < tail`
- `stored_type_inv(deposited, cur_idx, cell_ids[log_entry_idx(cur_idx, buffer_size)], ul_inst)`
- Deposits the `StoredType` into `contents[cur_idx]`
- Updates `alive_bits[log_entry_idx(cur_idx, buffer_size)] = log_entry_alive_value(cur_idx, buffer_size)`
- Produces `combiner[nid] == Appending { cur_idx: cur_idx + 1, tail }`

The ghost token `g` (the old `alive_bits` token for this slot) gets consumed and replaced by the new alive value. This explains why `g` is both read and written.

---

### Error 4 — Lines 1316-1320: `atomic_with_ghost!` for store on `slog[log_idx].alive` — invariant not satisfied

This is the *same* error as #3 above. The `BufferEntry::alive` atomic invariant requires:
```
g.instance_id() == cyclic_buffer_instance@.id()
g.key() == cyclic_buffer_idx@
g.value() === v  // the boolean alive bit
```

After calling `store(m)`, the new value `v = m` (a bool). But `g` still has the old value (the old alive bit). We need to fire `append_flip_bit` which swaps the alive bit token.

**Fix:** Same as Error 3 — fire `append_flip_bit` inside this block, consuming the old `alive_bits` token and producing a new one with `value == log_entry_alive_value(cur_idx, buffer_size)`.

---

### Errors 5-6 — Lines 1629-1632 and 1698-1700: `execute` function loop invariants

**Error 5 (line 1629):** The outer loop invariant at start:
```rust
ghost_data.combiner@.value().is_Placed() ==> {
    &&& ghost_data.combiner@.value().get_Placed_queued_ops() == request_ids
    &&& combiner.value().get_Loop_queued_ops() == request_ids
},
```
This requires that when `combiner` enters the loop, it's in `CombinerState::Loop` state. But `combiner` starts as `Ready` or `Placed` (from `execute_pre`). The transition to `Loop` happens via `exec_load_local_version` (Placed → LoadedLocalVersion) and then `exec_load_global_head` (LoadedLocalVersion → Loop).

The `local_version` load (lines 1592-1598) and `global_tail` load (lines 1599-1605) must fire these UL transitions.

**Fix for `local_versions[nid]` load (lines 1592-1598):**
```rust
let mut local_version =
    atomic_with_ghost!(
    &self.local_versions[nid].0 => load();
    returning ret;
    ghost g => {
        // g: (UnboundedLog::local_versions<DT>, CyclicBuffer::local_versions<DT>)
        // Fire exec_load_local_version: Placed -> LoadedLocalVersion
        // Also fire CB reader_start: Idle -> Reading(Starting { start: g.1.value() })
        if combiner.value().is_Placed() {
            combiner = self.unbounded_log_instance.borrow().exec_load_local_version(
                nid as nat, &g.0, combiner);
            cb_combiner = self.cyclic_buffer_instance.borrow().reader_start(
                nid as nat, &g.1, cb_combiner);
        }
    }
);
```

**Fix for `tail` load (lines 1599-1605):**
```rust
let global_tail =
    atomic_with_ghost!(
    &self.tail.0 => load();
    returning global_tail;
    ghost g => {
        // g: (UnboundedLog::tail<DT>, CyclicBuffer::tail<DT>)
        // Fire exec_load_global_head: LoadedLocalVersion -> Loop
        // Fire CB reader_enter: Reading(Starting) -> Reading(Range { start, end: g.1.value(), cur: start })
        if combiner.value().is_LoadedLocalVersion() {
            combiner = self.unbounded_log_instance.borrow().exec_load_global_head(
                nid as nat, &g.0, combiner);
            cb_combiner = self.cyclic_buffer_instance.borrow().reader_enter(
                nid as nat, &g.1, cb_combiner);
        }
    }
);
```

After these, `combiner` is `Loop { queued_ops, lversion: local_version, tail: global_tail, idx: 0 }` and `cb_combiner` is `Reading(Range { start: local_version, end: global_tail, cur: local_version })`.

**Error 6 (lines 1698-1700):** In the inner `while !is_alive` loop:
```rust
is_alive ==> cb_combiner.value().get_Reading_0().is_Guard(),
is_alive ==> cb_combiner.value().get_Reading_0().get_Guard_cur() == local_version,
```

After `is_alive` becomes true (the alive bit matched), `cb_combiner` needs to be in `Reading(Guard { cur: local_version, ... })`. This transition is `reader_guard`. The `alive` load (lines 1711-1716) must fire `reader_guard` when the entry is alive.

**Fix for `slog[phys_log_idx].alive` load in inner loop (lines 1711-1716):**
```rust
let alive_bit =
    atomic_with_ghost!(
    &self.slog[phys_log_idx].alive => load();
    returning alive_bit;
    ghost g => {
        // g: CyclicBuffer::alive_bits<DT>
        // If this entry is alive (g.value() == is_alive_value), fire reader_guard
        if g.value() == is_alive_value {
            cb_combiner = self.cyclic_buffer_instance.borrow().reader_guard(
                nid as nat, cb_combiner);
            // Note: reader_guard requires:
            //   combiner[nid] == Reading(Range { start, end, cur })
            //   alive_bits[log_entry_idx(cur, buffer_size)] == log_entry_alive_value(cur, buffer_size)
            //   and cur < end
        }
    });
```

---

### Error 7 — Lines 1848-1856 (`find_min_local_version`): invariant before and after loop

**Loop invariant:**
```rust
g_cb_comb_new.value().is_AdvancingHead(),
g_cb_comb_new.value().get_AdvancingHead_idx() == idx,
g_cb_comb_new.value().get_AdvancingHead_min_local_version() == min_local_version,
```

**Before the loop (idx == 1 after the initialization):** `g_cb_comb_new` must be `AdvancingHead { idx: 1, min_local_version: local_versions[0] }`.

**The initial `local_versions[0]` load** (lines 1841-1846) must fire `advance_head_start`, which transitions CB combiner from `Idle → AdvancingHead { idx: 1, min_local_version: local_versions[0] }`:

```rust
let mut min_local_version =
    atomic_with_ghost!(
    &self.local_versions[0].0 => load();
    returning ret;
    ghost g => {
        // g: (UnboundedLog::local_versions<DT>, CyclicBuffer::local_versions<DT>)
        // Fire advance_head_start: Idle → AdvancingHead { idx: 1, min_local_version: g.1.value() }
        // advance_head_start requires:
        //   combiner[nid] == Idle
        //   have local_versions >= [0 => local_head_0]
        g_cb_comb_new = self.cyclic_buffer_instance.borrow().advance_head_start(
            g_node_id, &g.1, g_cb_comb_new);
    });
```

**Inside the loop body (lines 1861-1866):** The `local_versions[idx]` load must fire `advance_head_next`, which transitions `AdvancingHead { idx, min } → AdvancingHead { idx: idx+1, min: min(min, local_versions[idx]) }`:

```rust
let cur_local_tail =
    atomic_with_ghost!(
    &self.local_versions[idx].0 => load();
    returning ret;
    ghost g => {
        // g: (UnboundedLog::local_versions<DT>, CyclicBuffer::local_versions<DT>)
        // Fire advance_head_next: AdvancingHead { idx, min } → AdvancingHead { idx+1, min(min, g.1.value()) }
        g_cb_comb_new = self.cyclic_buffer_instance.borrow().advance_head_next(
            g_node_id, &g.1, g_cb_comb_new);
    });
```

After this, `g_cb_comb_new.value().get_AdvancingHead_idx() == idx + 1` and `get_AdvancingHead_min_local_version() == min(min_local_version, cur_local_tail)`, which matches the invariant after `if cur_local_tail < min_local_version { min_local_version = cur_local_tail }` and `idx = idx + 1`.

---

### Error 8 — Line 1468: `head` store invariant not satisfied

**Location:** `advance_head` function, after `find_min_local_version` returns and we store the new head value.

```rust
atomic_with_ghost!(
    &self.head.0 => store(min_local_version);
    update old_val -> new_val;
    ghost g => {
    });
```

The `head` atomic invariant: `g: CyclicBuffer::head<DT>` with `g.value() == v`. After `store(min_local_version)`, the new value is `min_local_version`, so `g` must be updated to `value == min_local_version`. This requires firing `advance_head_finish` which:
- Requires `combiner[nid] == AdvancingHead { idx, min_local_version }` with `idx == num_replicas`
- Updates `head = min_local_version`
- Transitions to `Idle`

**Fix:**
```rust
atomic_with_ghost!(
    &self.head.0 => store(min_local_version);
    update old_val -> new_val;
    ghost g => {
        // g: CyclicBuffer::head<DT>
        // Fire advance_head_finish: AdvancingHead { idx == num_replicas, min_local_version }
        //   → Idle, with head updated to min_local_version
        // cb_combiner is AdvancingHead with idx == num_replicas (returned by find_min_local_version)
        let tracked (new_cb_combiner, new_head) =
            self.cyclic_buffer_instance.borrow().advance_head_finish(
                cb_combiner.key(), cb_combiner, g);
        cb_combiner = new_cb_combiner;
        g = new_head;
    });
```

Note: `find_min_local_version` returns `cb_combiner` with `value().is_AdvancingHead()` and `get_AdvancingHead_idx() == self.num_replicas`, which is exactly the precondition for `advance_head_finish`.

---

### Error 9 — Lines 1389 / 1567: postconditions not satisfied

**Line 1389 (`advance_head` ensures):**
```rust
res@.advance_head_post(ghost_data@, replica_token.id_spec(), ...)
```
`advance_head_post` requires `cb_combiner@.value() == pre.cb_combiner@.value()` — the cb_combiner value must return to its original state (`Idle`, since `advance_head_pre` requires `is_Idle()`). This is satisfied once:
- Error 8 is fixed (the `head` store fires `advance_head_finish` which returns `cb_combiner` to `Idle`)
- Error 7 is fixed (so the `head` store can fire `advance_head_finish`)

**Line 1567 (`execute` ensures):**
```rust
result@.execute_post(ghost_data@, replica_token@, ...)
```
`execute_post` requires `cb_combiner@.value() == pre.cb_combiner@.value()` (Idle). After the execute loop completes with `local_version == global_tail`:
- CB combiner is in `Reading(Range { cur == global_tail, end == global_tail })`
- Must fire `reader_finish` to return to `Idle` and update `local_versions`

The `local_versions[nid]` store (lines 1799-1802) must fire:
1. `exec_finish` (UL: UpdatedVersion → Ready, updates local_versions)
2. `reader_finish` (CB: Reading(Range { cur==end }) → Idle, updates local_versions)

**Fix for `version_upper_bound` fetch_max (lines 1795-1798):**
```rust
atomic_with_ghost!(
    &self.version_upper_bound.0 => fetch_max(global_tail);
    ghost g => {
        // g: UnboundedLog::version_upper_bound<DT>
        // Fire exec_update_version_upper_bound: Loop -> UpdatedVersion
        combiner = self.unbounded_log_instance.borrow().exec_update_version_upper_bound(
            nid as nat, combiner);
        // The fetch_max updates g.value() to max(old, global_tail)
        // The UL invariant requires g.value() == new atomic value
        // exec_update_version_upper_bound updates version_upper_bound to max(pre.version_upper_bound, tail)
    });
```

**Fix for `local_versions[nid]` store (lines 1799-1802):**
```rust
atomic_with_ghost!(
    &self.local_versions[nid].0 => store(global_tail);
    ghost g => {
        // g: (UnboundedLog::local_versions<DT>, CyclicBuffer::local_versions<DT>)
        // Fire UL exec_finish: UpdatedVersion -> Ready, updates local_versions[nid] = global_tail
        // Fire CB reader_finish: Reading(Range { cur==end }) -> Idle, updates local_versions[nid] = global_tail
        let tracked (ul_lv, cb_lv) = g;
        let tracked (new_ul_lv, new_combiner) =
            self.unbounded_log_instance.borrow().exec_finish(nid as nat, combiner, ul_lv);
        combiner = new_combiner;
        let tracked (new_cb_lv, new_cb_combiner) =
            self.cyclic_buffer_instance.borrow().reader_finish(nid as nat, cb_combiner, cb_lv);
        cb_combiner = new_cb_combiner;
        g = (new_ul_lv, new_cb_lv);
    });
```

---

## Summary Table

| Error | Location | Root Cause | Fix |
|-------|----------|------------|-----|
| 1 | Line 1190 | `cb_combiner` is `Idle` when `advance_tail_abort` needs `AdvancingTail` | Fire `advance_tail_start` inside the `head` load block (line 1176) |
| 2 | Lines 1234-1240 | CAS block empty; CB/UL state not updated on success/failure | On success: fire `unbounded_log_append_entries` + `advance_tail_finish`; on failure: fire `advance_tail_abort` |
| 3 | Line 1270 | `cb_combiner.cur_idx` not incremented after `store(m)` | Fire `append_flip_bit` in the `store(m)` alive-bit block |
| 4 | Lines 1316-1320 | `alive_bits` token not updated after alive store | Same fix as #3: `append_flip_bit` swaps the alive token |
| 5 | Lines 1629-1632 | `combiner` not in `Loop` state at loop entry | Fire `exec_load_local_version` in local_version load; `exec_load_global_head` in tail load |
| 6 | Lines 1698-1700 | `cb_combiner` not in `Guard` state when `is_alive` is true | Fire `reader_guard` in the alive-bit load when the bit matches |
| 7 | Lines 1848-1856 | `g_cb_comb_new` not `AdvancingHead` at/in loop | Fire `advance_head_start` in `local_versions[0]` load; `advance_head_next` in each loop iteration's load |
| 8 | Line 1468 | `head` token not updated after `store(min_local_version)` | Fire `advance_head_finish` in the `head` store block |
| 9 | Lines 1389/1567 | Postconditions cascade from the above missing transitions | Fixed transitively by fixes 1-8; also need `exec_update_version_upper_bound` in `fetch_max` and `exec_finish`+`reader_finish` in `local_versions` store |

The critical insight throughout is that **every `atomic_with_ghost!` block must fire the appropriate state machine transition** that corresponds to the operation being performed, updating both the `UnboundedLog` and `CyclicBuffer` ghost tokens to maintain the atomic invariants and advance the protocol state.
</task_result>
</task>
